name: Adaptive practice coach
description: Listens to you play via mic and rewrites tomorrow's plan based on what was weak. Existing apps give feedback in the moment — none adjust the plan.

name: Spaced repetition for guitar
description: Anki for repertoire: licks, chord shapes and songs resurface on a schedule based on how well you actually played them (mic-verified).

name: Passive Practice Auto-Logger & Wrapped
description: Detects instrument playing via mic activity, logs sessions locally, and generates shareable Wrapped summaries (#3 + #4).

name: "Guitar Wrapped"
description: Year-in-review of your playing: hours, streaks, fastest progression, most-played keys, before/after clips. Built to be shared.

name: Guitarist Weakness Radar & Skill Assessment
description: Diagnostic 5-axis spider chart skill assessment for guitarists. Pinpoint technique weak spots and get an algorithmic practice prescription.

name: Song-first curriculum
description: Name the song you want to play; the app reverse-engineers the technique tree you need and builds the path. Your goal, not a generic syllabus.

name: Exam prep companion
description: Rockschool/ABRSM/Trinity graded-guitar syllabus tracker with sight-reading and aural drills. ⚠ track the public syllabus, host nothing licensed

name: Jazz comping trainer
description: Scores your voicings and time, then comps with you (piano/bass) through the changes. Practice partners that react are the missing half.

name: Triad Inversion Visual Trainer
description: Master 3-note triad inversions across strings 1-2-3 and 2-3-4 with interactive visual diagrams, audio arpeggiator, and flashcard quizzes.

name: Adaptive speed trainer
description: Detects your clean max tempo for a lick through the mic, ramps in safe increments, backs off when it hears slop. A closed-loop metronome.

name: Picking-motion coach
description: Phone camera (free MediaPipe hand tracking) + audio flags inefficient pick motion, tension and anchoring problems.

name: Posture webcam coach
description: Flags the wrist angles, shoulder hike and neck position that cause tendonitis. Cheap to build now, nobody's done it.

name: Fretboard Memory Palace
description: Spaced-repetition fretboard note trainer with rapid-fire sprint mode, audio physical pluck synthesis, and visual interactive 22-fret neck.

name: Rhythm-first beginner path
description: Time before chords: clap/tap/play-along rhythm course scored by mic. Real pedagogy, and the whole niche is unserved.

name: Fingerstyle & Travis Picking Bootcamp
description: Master alternating bass thumb independence with interactive animated tabs, syncopated pinch patterns, and tempo ramps.

name: Barre Chord Survival & Strength Gym
description: Overcome the #1 beginner guitar wall. Biomechanical leverage ergonomics, 6-string knuckle pressure diagnostics, and isometric endurance timers.

name: Slide intonation visualizer
description: Shows cents deviation live while you glide. Teaches slide by eye and ear at once; tiny market, zero competition.

name: Kids' guitar adventure
description: Mic-scored quests with a cartoon fretboard, 10 minutes a day, parent progress emails. Nobody owns ages 6–9.

name: Senior-friendly beginner app
description: Giant type, slow tempos, chair-friendly posture, arthritis-adapted chord choices. Underserved and growing market.

name: Classroom mode (music schools)
description: Teacher dashboard for 20 students: who practiced, who's stuck, auto-generated homework. Schools pay; students pay nothing.

name: Practice accountability pods
description: Four-person cohorts with streak targets and a shared feed. Sticky because of the people, not the points.

name: "Play in public in 30 days"
description: Outcome-driven program: five stage-ready songs plus a performance simulator at the end. People pay for outcomes, not lessons.

name: Performance-Pressure Simulator
description: Rehearse with realistic crowd noise, random bar distractions, red-light camera mode, and strict one-take recovery rules.

name: White-label app for teachers
description: Any YouTube guitar teacher spins up their own branded lesson app — their videos, their students — in an afternoon. You take a cut.

name: Daily riff streak
description: Three-minute micro-lesson delivered by notification, scored by mic. The Wordle-ification of guitar practice.

name: Personal A&R credential
description: Pass a real skill battery, earn a shareable "ready to gig / ready for jazz band" badge. Credentials monetize; levels motivate.

name: Public-Domain Songbook Generator
description: Turn out-of-copyright traditional and classical melodies into clean, playable guitar tablature.

name: CC-licensed tab commons
description: Wikipedia-for-tabs with licensing baked in from day one: contributors publish under Creative Commons, reputation and proofreading economics included.

name: "Genius for guitar tabs"
description: annotated tabs: hover a lick and get theory, technique, tone notes, historical context, player commentary, community video links. Tab sites are still 2004-quality documents.

name: Audio → tab for your own recordings
description: Play it or load your file, get a rough tab of what you actually played. Basic Pitch does the note extraction; you add the guitar logic.

name: YouTube Smart Practice Looper
description: Practice any YouTube guitar solo or lesson with seamless A/B micro-looping, pitch-preserved slowdown (50%-100%), and measure bookmarks.

name: Tab error detection
description: crowdsourced + algorithm cross-check of Ultimate Guitar's user tabs: flag wrong chords against audio analysis, show a "confidence score" per section. Sells trust, not content.

name: Tab copyright grader for authors
description: Upload your transcription plus the audio and learn whether you've copied a published arrangement or made an original transcription — plus a licensing checklist.

name: Official-license aggregator
description: One search shows where to legally buy each song's tab (Musicnotes, Sheet Music Direct, Hal Leonard) with prices compared. Referral revenue, zero rights risk.

name: Fretboard Chart Simplifier
description: Turn complex jazz, R&B, and neo-soul chords into easy 3-note Freddie Green shell voicings and ergonomic acoustic shapes.

name: One-string / accessibility tabs
description: Simplifies any melody into note-by-note playable lines for kids, beginners and players with limited mobility. Teachers order these in bulk.

name: Nashville Number & Capo Intelligence
description: Transposition engine between chord charts and NNS with interactive SVG fretboard capo visualization (#37 + #39).

name: Capo intelligence
description: Explains visually on a fretboard: "capo 3, play G shapes, actual key Bb." The theory beginners never get, packaged as one widget.

name: Alternative Tuning Chord & Drone Library
description: Chord library and acoustic drone engine for DADGAD, Open G, Open D, Drop D, and Open C alternative tunings.

name: Tab + video sync editor
description: A creator tool: upload performance video and tab, get them scrolling in perfect sync for lessons and social clips.

name: Vertical tab videos
description: 15-second riff format with tab animating over the clip, made for Reels/TikTok. A content format and a distribution channel in one. ⚠ creators use their own material

name: Handwritten tab digitizer
description: Photo of your paper tab → clean digital tab. Every old-school player and luthier has boxes of this stuff.

name: Chord Chart Cleaner & Formatter
description: Reflows messy forum chord tabs and ChordPro text into clean, printable, transposable lead sheets.

name: Smart songbook binder
description: All your charts — PDF, ChordPro, text, screenshots — in one local library with transposition, autoscroll and foot-pedal control. Local-first means no server bills.

name: Fingering advisor
description: Import MusicXML, get recommended positions and fingerings for your hand size and level. Classical guitarists do this by hand for hours.

name: On-Instrument Ear Trainer
description: Generates intervals and phrases, listens to your guitar response via mic, and scores accuracy.

name: Functional ear trainer for guitar
description: Scale-degree training, but the answer is a fretboard position in your key of the day, with guitar timbre. Functional Ear Trainer is piano-shaped.

name: Call-and-response phrase game
description: The app plays a two-bar phrase; you echo it. Phrases grow in length and harmonic complexity. Jazzers pay teachers for exactly this.

name: "Name that riff" multiplayer quiz
description: guess the song from a riff; play along to prove it. Trivially viral, genuinely fun at parties and on Twitch.

name: Pocket & Groove Scoring Engine
description: Measure guitar rhythm micro-timing jitter (ahead vs behind the beat) with quantitative pocket scoring and groove feel classification.

name: The "Listening" Metronome
description: Smart practice metronome that mutes itself when you play in the pocket, and clicks back on the moment you drift off tempo.

name: Polyrhythm playground
description: 3:2, 4:3, clave, son, rumba patterns over generated grooves, scored. Rhythm-section players would pay immediately.

name: Subdivision trainer
description: 8ths → 16ths → triplets → swing with a visual pulse and error highlighting. Answers "why do I rush every solo."

name: Take timing analyzer
description: Analyze a recording you made: bar-by-bar rush/drag heatmap and the exact bars to loop next session.

name: Volume & Hearing Safety Meter
description: Real-time microphone dB estimate with rehearsal exposure dosage alerts and safe listening budgets.

name: Closed-Loop Intonation Diagnostic
description: Measures open vs. 12th fret pitch drift to diagnose truss rod, nut slot, or saddle adjustments.

name: String Bend Accuracy Trainer
description: Real-time YIN pitch tracking displaying cents deviation with a 2-second hold-to-pass rule.

name: Vibrato coach
description: Measures rate, width and consistency of your vibrato against reference profiles. Unbelievably niche, unbelievably loved by blues players.

name: Transcription bootcamp
description: Stems unmute progressively as you correctly identify chord changes by playing them. Learn songs by ear as an actual workout.

name: "How Do I Get This Tone?" Recipe Finder
description: Instant tone recipes for iconic guitar solos and songs with exact pickup selector positions, amp tone stack dials, and pedal chains.

name: Browser Amp Sim & Modular FX Chain
description: Full virtual rig in the browser with drag-and-drop pedals and shareable preset URLs.

name: Pedalboard planner that listens
description: Plan the board, then A/B your rig before and after a proposed change via EQ-matched simulation of your own recording.

name: Tone-capture compare
description: Record a dry DI, run it through your profiler/plugin, and A/B against the original with a residual-error readout. Pro-grade nerd tool.

name: IR (impulse response) manager & marketplace
description: organize, audition, and buy cab sims; preview before buying via a free demo DI. Existing IR marketplaces have terrible UX.

name: Preset exchange + converter
description: Share presets across modelers and plugins with community mappings. Ties directly into #220's portability hub.

name: Settings database by song
description: Community-verified amp and pedal settings for famous songs, with audio proof and version votes. "Sultans of Swing = 420 ms, 30% mix."

name: Gear A/B blind test site
description: Two clips, everyone guesses which is the $3,000 rig. Results feed a public database of whether gear actually sounds different.

name: "Is this gear worth it for me" advisor
description: Your genre, room, volume limits, budget and current rig in — scored recommendations with reasons and used prices out. Decision support, not listings.

name: Apartment-volume tone solutions
description: What your tone sounds like at 65 dB, with attenuation, load-box and headphone options ranked. The urban player's #1 constraint.

name: Pedal price watch + deal scorer
description: alerts with "this is 18% below the 90-day median for this pedal in this condition" + condition-adjusted fair value. Reverb's new-listings firehose exists; *judgment* doesn't.

name: Gear Flips Tracker
description: Buy/sell ledger with shipping, platform fees, net profit, and hourly rate calculations.

name: Interactive Guitar Wiring Diagram Generator
description: Interactive guitar wiring schematics with 5-way blade switch simulation, color-coded pickup wire matrix, and bill of materials.

name: Guitar mod visualizer
description: Preview hardware, pickup and finish swaps on your guitar, with a note on resale impact. A Kisekae-style builder that's modern and shareable.

name: Parts compatibility checker
description: "Will this neck fit this body?" — structured fit rules for partscaster builders. Unglamorous, huge search demand, affiliate revenue.

name: Complete Guitar Setup Wizard
description: Interactive step-by-step guitar setup wizard diagnosing neck relief, bridge action, intonation, and pickup height in luthier order of operations.

name: String-Life Tracker
description: Per-guitar string change logs (brand, gauge, date, play hours) with change-due alerts and tone degradation warnings.

name: Humidity & climate log
description: Free weather API + manual readings track the climate your guitars live in and warn before cracking season. ⚠ no hardware required

name: Tone diary
description: Sixty seconds recorded per session, tagged with rig, room and settings, later searchable as "that clean sound from March."

name: Pedalboard Cost & Power Planner
description: Pick pedals, cables, and power supplies with current draw calculation (mA) and isolated power warnings.

name: Modeler translation explainer
description: Shows how a real amp's signal chain maps to your modeler's blocks, so you recreate tones by understanding instead of copying numbers.

name: Hum-to-Chords Idea Vault
description: Hum or whistle a vocal melody into your mic; extracts notes in real-time and generates matching chord progressions with audio preview.

name: Voice memo → lead sheet
description: Hum it, get a lead sheet with chords and a simple arrangement. Transcription + chord detection + notation in one flow.

name: Progression generator by feeling
description: "Melancholic but hopeful, DADGAD, for a wedding" → five progressions with fingerings, audio, and why they work. Emotionally searchable theory.

name: Song structure sandbox
description: Drag intro/verse/chorus/bridge blocks and hear generated backing in your key. Write by arrangement first, chords second.

name: Generated Backing Tracks (Procedural Band)
description: Text chord chart in → sample-accurate AudioWorklet drums, bass, and keys with zero copyright fees.

name: Adaptive backing band
description: A virtual band that follows your tempo and dynamics instead of forcing a grid. Start with chord-following; the full adaptive version is the hard, valuable version.

name: Playlist key & tempo scanner
description: Scan a list of songs for keys, tempos and capo suggestions, then plan a set order that flows. Brides and bandleaders both want this.

name: Set-energy planner
description: Models the emotional arc of a live set: warns about three slow songs in a row, suggests key transitions that won't wreck your singer.

name: Arrangement adapter
description: "I'm a solo acoustic act — adapt this six-piece song" → an arrangement for voice and guitar with part reduction suggestions.

name: Lyric & Chord Sheet Designer
description: Stage-glanceable chart designer with large chords, color-coded sections, and no mid-song page turns.

name: Covers-licensing planner
description: Helps you license covers correctly per venue and streaming platform, tracked per song. Boring but real — and nobody wants to build it.

name: Moodboard → tone brief
description: Three reference tracks in, a shooting brief out: tempo range, tone targets, arrangement references your bandmates will actually understand.

name: Collaboration whiteboard
description: A shared song workspace — charts, lyric edits, phone recordings, version history. Google Docs for songs, built properly.

name: Riff variation engine
description: Record four bars; get ten variations (rhythmic displacement, octave, inversion, modal shift) as tab and audio. A writing partner that never judges.

name: Lyric stress checker
description: Paste lyrics and melody; see where syllable stresses fight the rhythm. Songwriting's most-audible, least-taught mistake.

name: Jamulus front-end
description: A polished social layer over the free open-source low-latency jam engine: rooms, genres, skill tags, scheduled jams. ⚠ rooms host peer-to-peer; wired connections only

name: Jam-session map
description: Open mics, blues jams and porch pickers near you with level labels ("beginner-safe") and check-ins so you don't walk into an empty bar.

name: Bandmate finder with a trust layer
description: Filter by influences, gear, availability, ambition — and reliability history from past bands. Fixes the actual failure mode of every band.

name: One-click virtual open mic
description: scheduled 10-minute video slots, low-latency audio path, audience tipping, replay clips. COVID-era platforms died; the habit of watching strangers play survived on TikTok Live. Pick the format up properly.

name: Rehearsal room finder
description: Local studio inventory with hourly booking requests and gear lists. Still done by phone calls in 2026.

name: Gig marketplace for amateurs
description: wedding/corporate/bar gigs posted, local bands bid, contracts and deposits handled. Vast, fragmented, done on WhatsApp.

name: Dep musician network
description: "Our guitarist is sick tonight" → verified local deps who know the 40-song covers set, ranked by how fast they learn.

name: Setlist co-editor for the band
description: Everyone edits in real time, votes on songs, and the drummer always has the final version. Small, sharp, underserved.

name: Rehearsal Audio Splitter & Song Marker
description: Drop your band rehearsal recording or phone audio; automatically splits long takes into individual songs using silence detection with BPM & key tagging.

name: Band admin bot
description: Gigs, payouts, mileage, gear checklists and availability as a bot inside Telegram or Discord. ⚠ free platforms only — not WhatsApp

name: Multi-track rehearsal recorder
description: Record rehearsal through an interface with per-member stems, auto-mixed, private share links ("here's your bass line, flat in the chorus").

name: Live stream kit for local gigs
description: Phone + interface + this app → multi-cam stream with a proper audio mix, a tip link and a venue page. Bars want streams; nobody sells them a package.

name: Busker toolkit
description: Repertoire manager, tip QR, set timer, spot rotation map, weather and foot-traffic forecasts. A real community with zero purpose-built software.

name: Tribute-band toolkit
description: Reference recordings, note-perfect tab, tone notes, costume checklists and stage plots. Tiny niche, very high willingness to pay.

name: Find-a-teacher with trial automation
description: Search by genre, area, online/in-person and price; first lesson, booking, payment and reminders automated.

name: Music school open-house tool
description: Trial-class registration, instrument matching quiz for parents, follow-up sequences. B2B, boring, profitable.

name: Studio OS for independent teachers
description: Students, scheduling, invoicing, lesson notes, recordings, repertoire tracking and auto-generated weekly practice lists per student. The incumbents are Excel and email.

name: Self-Grading Guitar Homework Studio
description: Students record assignments against click tracks; automatically grades timing and generates instructor reports.

name: Student Repertoire & Progress Roadmap
description: Private guitar instructor dashboard. Track student repertoire, skill proficiencies, weekly lesson homework assignments, and printable practice cards.

name: Parent dashboard for kids' practice
description: Honest practice time (detected, not self-reported) plus printable star charts. Parents pay more than students do.

name: Classroom quiz show
description: Teacher projects a chord or rhythm question; students answer on phones and on their instruments. Kahoot, but for guitar class.

name: Recital & ensemble manager
description: Programs, group rehearsal schedules, sheet distribution and audience ticketing links for music schools.

name: Sub-cover marketplace
description: Teachers trade substitute coverage when sick; schools find emergency instructors. Small product, obvious pain.

name: Teacher's tab tool
description: Type in a piece; print four differentiated versions — tab, notation, simplified, one-string — for the students in the room.

name: Skill assessment service
description: A human pro reviews a 20-minute video and writes a three-month plan. Sells at $39–79 and scales with a bench of assessors.

name: White-label course platform
description: YouTube guitar teachers get their own membership site with lesson embedding, progress tracking, tab viewers and drip schedules.

name: Exam / audition mock service
description: A human examiner over video scores your mock graded exam like the real thing. High margin, zero inventory.

name: Music school lead-gen engine
description: SEO-optimized local pages ("guitar lessons in [city]") built for schools. Agency-style recurring revenue.

name: Arrangement service
description: Teachers commission school-appropriate arrangements of PD or licensed songs from a bench of arrangers. Fixes a weekly headache.

name: Repair Diagnostic Wizard
description: Interactive decision-tree troubleshooter for guitar buzz, high action, setup issues, and electronics symptoms with measurement guides.

name: Serial Number Decoder
description: Decode year, factory, and production batch across major brands with counterfeit anomaly flags.

name: Fake-detection assistant
description: Photo-guided checklist comparing your candidate against known authentics. Buyers pay per check; sellers use it as a badge.

name: Guitar Collection Manager
description: Local database for specs, serials, photos, maintenance history, and printable insurance schedules.

name: Valuation cross-check
description: Median of public sold prices and listings, condition-adjusted, with a trend line and an honest confidence range.

name: Estate liquidation helper
description: "Dad left 14 guitars and a workshop" → identify, value, photograph and list step by step, plus buyers who'll take the lot. Grief-adjacent, entirely unserved.

name: Luthier Workbench Toolkit
description: Professional luthier workbench toolkit with 12-TET fret placement calculator, printable under-string radius gauges, and nut slot depth calibration.

name: Repair lead matcher
description: "Needs a refret" → matched luthiers with wait times and price ranges. Reverb owns selling; nobody owns fixing.

name: Parts scavenger
description: Saved searches across public listings for the one 1963 tremolo arm you need, with alerts. Hobbyist-with-a-project has no good tool.

name: Vintage provenance tracker
description: Attach photos, receipts, service history and prior owners to a serial number. The Carfax for old guitars — ownership history raises resale value.

name: Insurance comparison (reduced)
description: Quote routing and collection-value inputs for instrument-specific policies. Standard home insurance excludes gigging gear; affiliate revenue.

name: Shop inventory syndication
description: Small shops get their inventory onto marketplaces and a Google-indexed storefront, auto-synced. Shops pay monthly; you fix a dying channel for them.

name: Shop events engine
description: Clinics, jam nights and repair days promoted to the local guitar population. Shops pay to fill rooms.

name: Guitar show calendar
description: The guitar-show circuit and local swap meets with a "worth the drive" filter. Community glue, sponsorship revenue.

name: Riff battles
description: Fifteen-second video riffs, head-to-head brackets, weekly themes. TikTok mechanics in a guitar container.

name: Daily Riff Streak & Speed Ladder
description: Daily riff challenge with progressive 50%-110% speed training and streak habit retention.

name: Tab karaoke
description: social play-along rooms where everyone plays the same song together on mute, scored, and the leaderboard updates live. Rocksmith's multiplayer, browser-based, no copy protection problems if the songs are yours.

name: Multiplayer fretboard quiz
description: Real-time "name this note / find this interval" battles with a global ladder. The fretboard game, but as a live sport.

name: Feedback game
description: Record a 60-second performance; scored by an audio model plus community votes, with sponsored weekly winners. ⚠ your own recordings, no licensed audio

name: Trophy room
description: Badges for verifiable achievements ("barre chords in every key", "five songs stage-ready") as shareable SVG trophies. Cheap to build, addictive to 12–24s.

name: Practice-with-me livestreams
description: Scheduled synchronized practice: everyone muted, playing together on a shared timer with a host. Body-doubling for guitarists. ⚠ free video platforms

name: Guess the guitarist
description: An audio quiz built from submitted recordings — "name the player from their vibrato." Community-fed, costs nothing to run.

name: Local guitar club OS
description: Run a meetup: RSVPs, theme nights, chord charts, member levels, photo feed. Meetup.com is generic; clubs are the real unit of community.

name: Riff swap
description: Send a four-bar riff to a stranger; they send back a layer — bass, harmony, drums. Collaborative music without needing a band.

name: Kids' band league
description: Teams of four (guitar/bass/drums/keys), weekly missions, inter-school competitions. Turns the app into a social program parents organize around.

name: Adaptive instrument software
description: Alternate tunings, tapping layouts and chord simplification for players with hand differences or one-handed players. Small market, real funding, real press. ⚠ software side only

name: Loop pedal companion app
description: manage loops, export them to your DAW, and visualize the layers; syncs with existing pedals via MIDI.

name: Robotic amp attenuator
description: nah, but the *software* version: profile your amp at bedroom volume and re-EQ it to match the sound it makes at 100 dB. The "apartment cab" app problem, solved by DSP.

name: Open tab format + viewer SDK
description: Format + metadata + embeddable viewer on top of the open alphaTab engine, so any independent site can host playable, properly-licensed tabs in one line of code.

name: Guitar genome
description: Crowdsourced spec database for every model: neck profile, weight, scale length, hardware — linked later to the pickup library (#71) and tone references. Built over years; becomes the reference everyone cites.

name: Capture trainer for humans
description: Turns "record a sweep and upload it" into a guided 10-minute flow: mic placement coaching, level and clipping checks, accuracy scoring. ⚠ basics now covered by free tools; the guidance layer is the gap

name: Capture quality score & vetting
description: Measurement-based ratings for captures — accuracy vs. source, noise floor, aliasing, dynamic-range drift — with a "proven" badge tier. The ecosystem's #1 complaint is digging through bad profiles.

name: Embeddable NAM player
description: Tone embeds for forum posts, articles and preset pages — hear a capture without installing anything. ⚠ partly eaten by TONE3000's in-app audition; the third-party web embed is what's left

name: Capture-format bridge
description: Best-effort cross-ecosystem porting by capture-by-listening: train a NAM model on another format's output. Not file conversion — measured matching.

name: Audio Interface Input Gain & Impedance Calibrator
description: Knob padding and input calibration for Focusrite, Apollo, and MOTU to hit standard -18.0 dBFS sweet spots.

name: Tone-lock matcher
description: Continuously matches your DI's tonal curve to a reference recording in real time. For cover bands and "sound like the record" practice sessions.

name: Bedroom-volume re-profiler
description: Capture your amp at 100 dB, then get a version corrected for how hearing changes at low volume — so headphones keep the perceived attack. Every apartment player's white whale.

name: Amp-in-the-room headphone sim
description: Modeled early reflections and room coupling to kill the "dry, in-my-head" feeling of headphone practice. Pairs with #177 and #211.

name: Live-failover rig host
description: Hot standby, crash auto-restart with crossfade, click-free patch switching, panic bypass. Fear of the laptop dying is why pros still tour with pedals. ⚠ ambitious build

name: Interactive Signal-Path Explainer
description: Hear and see why pedal order matters: Wah vs. Fuzz, Reverb pre/post Drive, and FX loop routing.

name: Guitar repair plugin
description: De-noises guitar specifically: finger squeaks, pick noise, fret-buzz clicks, chair creaks, string rattle. The expensive general tools damage tone trying; nobody made the $49 guitar-specific strip.

name: Hum & ground-loop killer
description: Adaptive 50/60 Hz fundamental-plus-harmonics suppression that learns the hum's fingerprint from the silent gaps and doesn't gut your highs. P90 and Strat players have waited decades.

name: Mix-ready DI channel strip
description: Gate → EQ → compressor → saturation → space, voiced for guitar and driven by a reference track. "Match the guitar balance of this mix" as one affordable plugin.

name: Humanized double / quad tracker
description: Turns one DI take into believable doubles with timing jitter, micro pitch/tone drift and pick-attack variance. Producers do this by hand; no first-class tool exists.

name: Preset loudness normalizer
description: Equalizes perceived loudness across every patch in your setlist. The live-set killer — switching from a clean Fender to a Recto shouldn't blow the room's head off.

name: Parallel-chain phase/latency aligner
description: Auto-aligns dry, re-amped, pedal-sim and reverb paths so parallel rigs stop comb-filtering. Still a manual stem-measuring chore today.

name: Feedback sim
description: Controlled musical feedback and sustain for headphones and DAW recording. ⚠ mono version exists (Blue Cat AcouFiend) — build the per-string/polyphonic version

name: ABX Double-Blind Audio Testing Rack
description: Scientific double-blind audio comparator with exact binomial p-value statistics to settle tone debates.

name: Re-amp session recall
description: Store DI + full chain + gain staging as a recallable package, byte-perfect years later, with batch re-amping and per-song notes.

name: "Sit in the mix" assistant
description: Analyzes the whole mix and adjusts the guitar bus to fit, explaining what it did and why. The explainability is the product — silent AI magic is already distrusted.

name: Chart-to-guitar performance
description: Give it a ChordPro chart and a style ("90s alt-rock, jangly, capo 4"); get a realistic, humanized part with correct voicings and positions. Reads your song instead of making you pick patterns.

name: Notation → performance renderer
description: Import MusicXML or a tab file; get a rendered performance with humanized timing, position-based timbre and legato/slide noise. Game-changer for composers and tab-video channels.

name: Adaptive comping instrument
description: A virtual guitarist that follows you — your tempo, your dynamics, your changes — and comps underneath in real time. Hard to build; the demo alone would break the internet.

name: Guitar → Tab on Your Own Takes
description: Converts monophonic audio takes into playable guitar tablature with fret-hand position logic.

name: Producer guitar-in-a-box
description: For producers who don't play guitar: genre + era + role + a reference track → a convincing part with tone, constrained by guitar-idiomatic rules. Huge market (bedroom pop, hip-hop, sync).

name: Impossible-part preventer
description: Flags fret spans a human can't reach and suggests capo/tuning alternatives. Ships as a plugin or an API for virtual-instrument makers.

name: Performance-to-practice loop
description: Your DAW take → tab of what you played + timing/sloppiness report + tomorrow's practice loops built from your actual mistakes.

name: Setlist-first rig host
description: A simple, web-configured live host for a 40-song covers gig: per-song patches, tempo, notes, lyrics, footswitch navigation. ⚠ ambitious; deep-power hosts already exist

name: Setlist → tone auto-builder
description: Import your setlist; get a preset per song matched to the recorded tone, with pickup and volume-knob notes. "Sound like the record" in one click per song.

name: Practice-coach plugin
description: Inside your DAW: each take scored against the click (timing distribution, bend accuracy, dynamics), history stored, tomorrow's loop itinerary built. Rehearsal becomes measurable.

name: Studio guitar QC plugin
description: Scans a tracking session and reports tuning drift, hum changes, clipping, string-noise trends and inconsistent attack, as a written report for the producer.

name: Portable tone-patch standard
description: An open format describing an intended guitar sound — amp, cab, mic, settings, FX order, gain staging — independent of vendor, with converters. Standards plays are slow but whoever lands it owns the interchange layer.

name: License locker & migration assistant
description: Scans your machine, catalogs every plugin license, tracks which machine each lives on, warns before OS upgrades and generates the deactivation checklist. A pure painkiller.

name: Subscription optimizer
description: Tracks what you rent, estimates cost per actual use from your sessions, and tells you which subscriptions to cancel. Cost tools pay for themselves, so they convert.

name: Blind-test plugin finder
description: Purchase decisions via standardized blind comparisons against your current setup: "what you'd actually gain." Affiliate revenue that earns trust precisely because it's blind.

name: Preset market with in-browser audition
description: Hear any preset pack on a standard DI before buying, filtered by guitar, pickup and genre. Today preset packs are blind Zip files and a YouTube demo.

name: Device-Targeted NAM Capture Optimizer
description: Converts and optimizes Neural Amp Modeler captures for hardware pedals with fidelity reports.

name: Capture parameter extraction
description: Estimates "knobs" for a frozen capture — gain, tone stack mapping — so profiles become adjustable. Research-grade moonshot; whoever cracks it changes the category.

name: Binaural amp-in-room
description: HRTF-based rendering of a cab in a real room with head-turn compensation. Headphones stop sounding like skulls.

name: Round-trip latency coach
description: Measures your true round-trip latency, auto-aligns recorded vs. monitored signal, warns when a chain crosses the playability threshold. The community's most repeated frustration, solved with a utility.

name: Virtual pickup load & cable capacitance
description: Models input impedance, cable capacitance and pot loading so captures respond like they're plugged into a real guitar. The "why doesn't mine sound like the demo" fix.

name: Pickup-swap emulation
description: Re-voices a humbucker DI toward single-coil, P90 or filtertron response. ⚠ build from free IRs and published measurements — no buying pickups

name: String-aware noise gate
description: Gates only the hum and buzz bands using a learned fingerprint, leaving pick attack and the low E untouched. Generic gates can't do this.

name: Guitar-first ambient/freeze suite
description: Granular, shimmer, swell, freeze and glitch designed around an expression pedal and a footswitch instead of a mouse. Ambient and post-rock players have no home.

name: Acoustic WaveMap studio
description: The ToneDexter/VoicePrint trick as software: play pickup + mic, get a matched body-tone IR in the DAW, with blend and anti-feedback. ⚠ develop on user-submitted pickup+mic pairs

name: AI-Tab Fidelity Checker
description: Quality validation for AI-generated tabs: checks fretboard ergonomics, impossible spans, and audio sync.

name: Cross-Vendor Preset Portability Hub
description: Parameter mapping dictionary translating patches between Helix, Quad Cortex, Kemper, and plugins.

name: Foot-controller mapping OS
description: Auto-map any plugin's parameters to any MIDI foot controller with shareable community mapping files. Mapping hell is universal and currently solved by forum threads.

name: Setlist → device pack exporter
description: One click: setlist in, device-ready tone packs out (NAM pedal / ToneX / your plugin), loudness-normalized (#185), with tempo and notes. Built entirely on free open infrastructure.

name: Practice overlay for any recording
description: One window: stem isolation (free local Demucs), slow-down, loop trainer, optional AI tab overlay with confidence marks, notation export. Nobody merges practice with transcription confidence.

name: Teacher's tone-as-assignment
description: A teacher ships a tone chain plus tasks; the student records takes in-app and the teacher sees scored attempts before the lesson. A tone chain becomes homework.

name: Plugin CI/QA dashboard B2B
description: Automated plugin validation across formats, DAWs and operating systems via free CI, with crash telemetry and a compatibility matrix. Every indie dev rebuilds this badly.

name: Capture spec-sheet standard
description: Open metadata (gain staging, impedance, mic, cab, room, level reference) written into capture files and read by any player, so profiles sound right by default. An ecosystem young enough that a spec can still land.

name: Plugin / preset ROI tracker
description: Usage vs. spend dashboard for everything you own and rent. Turns subscription fatigue into a decision with numbers.

name: Pedal-circuit sandbox
description: Modular distortion design with component-level mods, a plain-language explainer of each change, and a community marketplace of user-designed dirt boxes. Education + ecosystem.

name: Certified blind-test service B2B
description: Brands pay for rigorous public blind tests of their products vs. competitors, with published methodology. Nobody in guitar audio is the RTINGS-grade authority yet.

name: Modeler onboarding courseware B2B
description: Interactive "learn your modeler in three hours" courses for the big hardware ecosystems, sold to the makers as official onboarding and to users as certification.

name: Local-first songbook organizer
description: All your charts, PDFs and screenshots in the browser, offline, no account, no server. You pay €0 per user forever; privacy becomes the marketing.

name: Crowdsourced data engine
description: Pick ONE dataset (PD arrangements, gear specs, NAM preset maps, tone references) and let users build your moat. Content costs nothing and compounds.

name: Zero-marginal-cost freemium
description: Architecture as product: all heavy processing on-device, so free users literally cost €0. You can be generous and ad-free forever — which is exactly why people will choose you over the ad-riddled incumbents.

name: Sponsored free access
description: Free for every player, paid for by brands and teachers: "this week's practice challenge is sponsored by [gear shop]." Zero cost to you, zero cost to users, real revenue.

name: Public-domain teaching academy
description: Old method books (Sor, Carcassi, Aguado) turned into an interactive free course track, with teachers contributing exercises for credit. No licenses, evergreen SEO.
